questions.question: For a function $f\colon A\to B$, which equation defines a left inverse $\ell\colon B\to A$ of $f$?
What does a right inverse $r\colon B\to A$ of a function $f\colon A\to B$ do?
options: It picks for each $b\in B$ an input $r(b)$ with $f(r(b))=b$.
It sends each element $x\in A$ back to $x$ itself.
It is $f$ itself with domain and codomain swapped.

questions.question: Suppose $f\colon A\to B$ and $\ell\colon B\to A$ satisfy $\ell\circ f=\operatorname{id}_A$. For $x,y\in A$, applying $\ell$ to $f(x)=f(y)$ gives which conclusion?
Suppose $f\colon A\to B$ and $r\colon B\to A$ satisfy $f\circ r=\operatorname{id}_B$. For an arbitrary $b\in B$, which input is guaranteed to be sent to $b$ by $f$?
Let $\ell,r\colon B\to A$ be a left inverse and a right inverse, respectively, of $f\colon A\to B$. Which equation completes the argument $\ell=\ell\circ(f\circ r)=(\ell\circ f)\circ r$?
For the inclusion $i\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2$, $i(t)=(t,0)$, which map is also a left inverse of $i$?
For $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $f(x)=\mathrm{e}^x$, which statement about one-sided inverses holds?
options: $f$ has neither a left nor a right inverse
$f$ has a left inverse but no right inverse
$f$ has a two-sided inverse on $\mathbb R$

questions.question: For $g\colon\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$, $g(x)=x^2$, which function is a right inverse of $g$?
For the projection $p\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$, $p(x,y)=x$, which map is a right inverse of $p$?
Which matrix $L$ is a left inverse of $A=\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\end{pmatrix}$, i.e. satisfies $LA=1$?
Let $f\colon A\to B$ be injective, with $A\ne\varnothing$. Define $\ell(f(x))=x$ on $f(A)$. How must $\ell$ be defined on $B\setminus f(A)$ to obtain a left inverse?
options: Assign any value in $A$ to each remaining point.
Leave it undefined at every remaining point.
Assign a distinct value in $A$ to each remaining point.
Assign each remaining point a preimage under $f$.

questions.question: Let $\ell\colon B\to A$ be a left inverse of $f\colon A\to B$, and write $P=f\circ\ell\colon B\to B$. What must hold for $P$?

Let $f\colon A\to B$ be surjective. Assume one element can be chosen from each nonempty fibre $f^{-1}(\{b\})$, where a fibre is the set of inputs sent to $b$. Which construction gives a right inverse $r\colon B\to A$?
options: Set $r(b)=a_0$ for every $b$, using any fixed $a_0\in A$.

questions.question: The row vector $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\end{pmatrix}$ defines the map $x\mapsto Ax$ from $\mathbb R^2$ to $\mathbb R$. For which $R$ does $AR=1$ hold?
Let $A=\{1,2,3\}$, $B=\{u,v\}$ and $f\colon A\to B$ satisfy $f(1)=f(2)=u$ and $f(3)=v$. Define the right inverse $r\colon B\to A$ by $r(u)=2$ and $r(v)=3$. How does $r$ behave?
options: One-to-one, but it misses an element of $A$
Onto $A$, but two inputs share an output

questions.question: For $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2$, $f(t)=(2t,\ t+1)$, which map is a left inverse of $f$?
Let $\ell_f$ be a left inverse of $f\colon A\to B$ and $\ell_g$ a left inverse of $g\colon B\to C$. Which map is a left inverse of $g\circ f$?
options: $\ell_g$ on its own, as it undoes $g$
None need exist for the composition

questions.question: For an injective $f\colon A\to B$, where $A$ has at least two elements, when is the left inverse of $f$ unique?
options: Only when $A$ and $B$ are finite sets
Never, as values can always be changed

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, which $2\times3$ matrix $L$ satisfies $LA=I_2$, where $I_2$ is the $2\times2$ identity matrix?
Let $1\le n<m$ and let $f\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$. At $a\in\mathbb R^n$, its Jacobian $Df(a)$ has rank $n$. Which statement follows?
options: $Df(a)$ has a right inverse, and $f$ maps a neighbourhood of $a$ onto a neighbourhood of $f(a)$ in $\mathbb R^m$.
$Df(a)$ has a left inverse, and $f$ is injective on some neighbourhood of $a$.
$Df(a)$ has a two-sided inverse, and $f$ is bijective between neighbourhoods in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb R^m$.
$Df(a)$ has neither one-sided inverse, and $f$ cannot be injective on any neighbourhood of $a$.
